cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), and he's talking straight to the LORD. His first words: 'To You, O LORD, I lift up my soul; in You, my God, I trust.' No small talk, no weather report, just his whole soul set right out on the counter.

cards.question: David asks the LORD not to let him be put to shame.

cards.text: Then David zooms out to everybody who waits for the LORD. And baker, I KNOW waiting, because I sat in a junk drawer so long the dust knew me by name.

cards.question: David says some people who wait for the LORD will still be put to shame.
David says those who wait for the LORD won't be put to shame. Who does he say WILL be disgraced?

cards.text: Then David goes from asking for cover to asking for lessons: 'Show me Your ways, O LORD; teach me Your paths.' Friend, some folks will circle the block for an HOUR before they ask for directions, and David just ASKS.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to guide him in His truth and teach him. What reason does David give?

answers.text: The LORD is the God of his salvation
David has always kept the law
David is the one ruling Israel

cards.question: David says he waits for the LORD all ___ long.

cards.text: Next, David turns to the past, and he asks the LORD to remember.

cards.question: What does David ask the LORD to remember?

answers.text: The LORD's compassion and loving devotion

cards.question: David asks the LORD to remember the sins of his youth.

cards.text: Instead he says, 'remember me according to Your loving devotion, because of Your goodness, O LORD.' Translation: don't go by MY track record, go by YOURS.

Then David stops talking TO the LORD and starts talking ABOUT Him: the LORD is good and upright. It's like hanging up with somebody great and turning to the whole room like, 'Y'all, let me TELL you about this One.'

cards.question: Because the LORD is good and upright, David says He shows ___ the way.
David says the LORD guides the humble in what is right.
David says all the LORD's ways are loving and faithful. To whom?

answers.text: Those who keep His covenant and decrees
Those who dwell within His holy city
Those who offer Him daily sacrifices

cards.text: Then David turns right back to the LORD and asks Him to forgive his iniquity, for the sake of His name.

cards.question: David tells the LORD his iniquity is only a small one.

cards.text: Then David throws out a question: 'Who is the man who fears the LORD?' And he doesn't wait around for hands to go up, friend, he goes RIGHT into what the LORD does for that man.

cards.question: What does David say the LORD will do for the man who fears Him?

answers.text: Instruct him in the path chosen for him
Give him a crown and a throne
Keep every trouble far away from him

cards.question: David says the soul of the man who fears the LORD will dwell in prosperity, and his ___ will inherit the land.

cards.text: Then David says the LORD confides in those who fear Him and reveals His covenant to them. The LORD, confiding in PEOPLE, and baker, my oven won't even tell me when a batch is done.
Now David says his eyes are always on the LORD, not sometimes, ALWAYS. Me, I can't keep my eyes on one batch for five minutes without burning it.

cards.question: David keeps his eyes on the LORD because the LORD will free his feet from the mesh.

cards.text: Then the psalm gets quiet, and David asks the LORD to turn to him and be gracious. Friend, this is the part of the song where the band drops out.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to turn to him and be gracious. What reason does David give?

cards.text: David asks to be freed from his distress, and for the LORD to consider his affliction and trouble. No 'I'm fine, thanks' here, baker, just the HONEST answer.

cards.question: David says the troubles of his heart are starting to shrink.
Along with considering his affliction and trouble, David asks the LORD to take away all his ___.
David asks the LORD to consider his enemies, and he says they are only a few.

cards.text: Then David asks the LORD to guard his soul and deliver him, and he says, 'let me not be put to shame…' That's the same request he opened with, friend, coming back around like an alarm on snooze.

cards.question: David asks the LORD to guard him and not let him be put to shame. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He takes refuge in the LORD
He built the LORD a temple

cards.question: David asks that integrity and uprightness preserve him.

cards.text: And then, in the very last line, David looks past himself. Friend, that's a man in trouble thinking about somebody else, and I can't even do that when my timer's going off.

cards.question: In the psalm's last line, who does David ask God to redeem from all its distress?
